question: Who approves a policy exception, and how long can it last?
reference_answer: The policy owner and COO must approve; the CEO handles requests involving the COO. Exceptions last no more than 90 days and require fresh review to renew.
required_facts: The policy owner and COO must approve; the CEO handles requests involving the COO.
Exceptions last no more than 90 days and require fresh review to renew.

reference_sections.title: Company Handbook and Policy Governance
reference_sections.heading: 3. Exceptions, assurance, and corpus map
reference_sections.text:
Exception procedure
Before deviating, the requester records the policy clause, business reason, risks, compensating controls, owner, and proposed expiry in the Policy Register. The policy owner and COO must approve; the CEO handles requests involving the COO. Exceptions last no more than 90 days and require fresh review to renew. No exception can authorize unlawful conduct, retaliation, falsification, or a contractual breach. An imminent safety emergency is handled immediately and documented afterward.

Assurance and corrective action
Owners review open exceptions monthly and sample compliance quarterly. Each finding has evidence, an accountable person, a due date, and closure verification by someone other than the implementer. The COO reviews overdue high-risk findings each week. Policy violations receive proportionate review under ETH-02, with an opportunity to respond; discipline is not automatic.

Corpus map
GOV-01 defines common rules. ETH-02 covers conduct and reporting. PPL-03 covers joining, leave, changes, and departure. WRK-04 covers remote work and safety. SEC-05 covers accounts and technology. DAT-06 covers information handling and retention. FIN-07 covers procurement and expenses. SUP-08 covers customer support and releases. INC-09 covers incidents and communication. BCP-10 covers continuity and recovery.

Evidence and retention
The Policy Register preserves approvals, version history, exceptions, and assurance findings for three years after supersession or closure under DAT-06. Every quarterly review records the sample, result, and follow-up. A reported weakness is treated as an improvement opportunity unless evidence warrants a conduct investigation.

question: Can I accept a $75 gift from a supplier without approval?
reference_answer: No; noncash gifts above $50 in aggregate from one source in a rolling 12 months require written COO approval before acceptance. Cash and cash-equivalent gifts are prohibited regardless of value; no gift may influence a decision.
required_facts: No; noncash gifts above $50 in aggregate from one source in a rolling 12 months require written COO approval before acceptance.

reference_sections.title: Code of Conduct and Speak-Up Procedure
reference_sections.heading: 1. Expected conduct and conflicts of interest
reference_sections.text:
Respectful work
Workers must treat colleagues, customers, applicants, and suppliers with dignity. Harassment, discrimination, threats, bullying, retaliation, and deliberate exclusion from work opportunities are prohibited. These expectations apply in meetings, chat, travel, customer locations, and company events. Managers must address observed concerns promptly and must not require an affected person to confront the subject before seeking help.

Honest business practices
Keep accurate time, expense, customer, and financial records. Never misrepresent product capabilities, conceal material service problems, or alter evidence. Company assets and confidential information may be used only for authorized work. Reasonable incidental personal use of devices is permitted under SEC-05 if it creates no security, cost, or performance issue.

Conflicts and gifts
Disclose outside employment, family relationships, financial interests, or personal relationships that could influence a business decision before participating in it. People Operations records a mitigation plan, such as recusal or an independent reviewer. Cash and cash-equivalent gifts are prohibited. Other gifts or hospitality above $50 in aggregate from one source in a rolling 12 months require written COO approval before acceptance. No gift may influence a decision, regardless of value.

Supplier example
An employee whose sibling owns a shortlisted supplier must disclose the relationship and leave the evaluation and approval process. FIN-07 still governs competition, diligence, and payment controls.

question: Who should receive a conduct complaint involving the CEO, and when should a reachable reporter be acknowledged?
reference_answer: Contact the designated board representative using the internal directory. The case owner acknowledges a reachable reporter within two business days.
required_facts: Contact the designated board representative using the internal directory.
The case owner acknowledges a reachable reporter within two business days.

reference_sections.title: Code of Conduct and Speak-Up Procedure
reference_sections.heading: 2. Reporting and case handling
reference_sections.text:
How to report
Report a concern to People Operations, an uninvolved manager, or the COO. If the concern involves the CEO, contact the designated board representative using the internal directory. Anonymous reports are accepted through the restricted conduct intake form, although missing contact details can limit follow-up. If there is immediate danger, seek local emergency assistance and follow INC-09 before routine case intake.

Intake procedure
The recipient forwards the concern to the restricted People Operations queue the same business day. The case owner acknowledges a reachable reporter within two business days, assesses immediate protection needs, and records the allegation, dates, available evidence, and any conflict of interest. Records must not go into a broadly visible Service Desk queue.

Investigation
An uninvolved investigator sets a proportionate scope, interviews relevant people separately, preserves original evidence, and allows the subject a fair opportunity to respond. Interim measures may include reporting-line changes or access restrictions; they are not findings of wrongdoing. People Operations targets completion within 20 business days and provides a progress update at least every ten business days if more time is needed.

Confidentiality
Share case information only with people who need it to assess, investigate, decide, or provide support. Do not promise absolute secrecy. Reporting does not prevent a person from seeking outside advice or contacting an appropriate authority.

question: How far ahead should I request foreseeable leave, when should my manager respond, and does silence mean approval?
reference_answer: Submit dates and a handover plan at least ten business days ahead when possible. The manager responds within three business days after checking coverage. Silence is not approval.
required_facts: Submit dates and a handover plan at least ten business days ahead when possible.
The manager responds within three business days after checking coverage.
Silence is not approval.

reference_sections.title: Employee Lifecycle and Leave Procedures
reference_sections.heading: 2. Working arrangements, leave, and role changes
reference_sections.text:
Hours and availability
Normal full-time scheduling is 40 hours per week, with individual arrangements documented in the employment agreement. Teams record agreed availability and coverage in their shared calendar. Additional hours require manager approval in advance where practicable and must be recorded accurately. People Operations applies the governing agreement and applicable requirements to pay and time-off treatment.

Leave procedure
Leave entitlement comes from the worker's agreement and applicable local rules; this corpus does not establish a universal statutory entitlement. For foreseeable leave, submit dates and a handover plan at least ten business days ahead when possible. The manager responds within three business days after checking coverage. A refusal must give a work-related reason and suggest alternatives. Do not treat silence as approval.

Unexpected absence
Notify the manager as soon as practicable, preferably before the scheduled start, without placing oneself at risk. If the manager is unavailable, contact People Operations. Share only the information needed to arrange absence and support; medical details belong in the restricted People Register, not a team channel.

Role and location changes
Before a transfer, the receiving manager requests a permission review and the former manager identifies access to remove. IT removes obsolete access by the effective date. Changes of country of work require advance People Operations and Finance review for employment, tax, and operational implications. WRK-04 governs the physical work environment.

question: Does our policy give every worker exactly 25 days of annual leave?
reference_answer: No universal entitlement is established by this corpus. Entitlement comes from the worker’s agreement and applicable local rules.

reference_sections.title: Remote Work, Workplace Safety, and Travel
reference_sections.heading: 1. Remote work and shared office rules
reference_sections.text:
Approved arrangements
Workers may use the shared office or an approved remote workspace consistent with their role and agreement. The manager documents the arrangement, expected availability, customer coverage, and equipment needs. A change of country requires PPL-03 review before work begins there. Remote work does not remove security, confidentiality, or attendance obligations.

Workspace controls
Use a company-managed device, lock the screen when away, and keep confidential discussions out of public hearing. Avoid shared household computers and unattended printing. Use an approved secure connection under SEC-05; do not connect company storage devices to untrusted equipment. Store paper records in a locked place and return them for approved destruction when no longer needed.

Office access and visitors
Workers use their assigned access credential and must not lend it or allow unknown people to follow them inside. Hosts register visitors, explain safety arrangements, escort them in nonpublic areas, and ensure departure is recorded. Visitors must not view customer records or use an employee's device. Report a lost credential immediately to IT and the office coordinator.

Equipment and costs
The manager approves necessary equipment through FIN-07. The asset register records custodian, serial number, issue date, and return status. Workers report faults and damage promptly; they must not arrange unauthorized repairs or dispose of equipment themselves.

question: Should I wait for manager approval or open a ticket before evacuating an unsafe office?
reference_answer: No; stop the unsafe activity and move to safety without creating further danger. Contact local emergency services when needed and follow building evacuation instructions; do not delay emergency action for approval or a ticket. Once safe, notify the manager or office coordinator.
required_facts: No; stop the unsafe activity and move to safety without creating further danger.
Contact local emergency services when needed and follow building evacuation instructions; do not delay emergency action for approval or a ticket.
Once safe, notify the manager or office coordinator.

reference_sections.title: Remote Work, Workplace Safety, and Travel
reference_sections.heading: 2. Safety and emergency response
reference_sections.text:
Routine prevention
Keep exits and walkways clear, use electrical equipment as intended, and report damaged cables, unstable furniture, leaks, or other hazards. Remote workers should arrange a stable chair, suitable screen height, adequate lighting, and regular movement breaks. The office coordinator maintains first-aid information and checks emergency instructions quarterly.

Immediate danger
Stop the unsafe activity. Move to safety without attempting a rescue that creates further danger. Contact local emergency services when needed and follow the building's evacuation instructions. Do not delay emergency action to open a ticket or obtain manager approval. Once safe, notify the manager or office coordinator so they can account for affected people.

Reporting procedure
Report a work-related injury, near miss, or significant hazard as soon as safe, normally the same day. Record what happened, location, time, affected activity, and immediate action; avoid speculation about blame. Sensitive medical information goes to People Operations. The office coordinator assigns corrective action and checks completion before reopening an unsafe area.

Escalation and learning
Serious injury, threats, evacuation, or loss of a worksite triggers INC-09 and may activate BCP-10. The COO reviews significant events within five business days after stabilization and shares practical lessons without unnecessary personal details. A worker may raise unresolved safety concerns through ETH-02 without retaliation.

question: Can staff share interactive logins, and how long can temporary access last without fresh approval?
reference_answer: Shared interactive logins are prohibited; use individual accounts. Temporary access expires within 30 days unless a fresh approval is recorded.
required_facts: Shared interactive logins are prohibited; use individual accounts.
Temporary access expires within 30 days unless a fresh approval is recorded.

reference_sections.title: Information Security and Access Management
reference_sections.heading: 1. Accounts, access, and devices
reference_sections.text:
Access principles
Use individual accounts and the least access needed for the approved role. Shared interactive logins are prohibited. Service accounts must have a named owner, defined purpose, approved permissions, and managed secrets. Multifactor authentication is required for email, remote access, administrative tools, and customer-data systems. Privileged and everyday activity must use separate accounts.

Request and approval
The manager opens a Service Desk request identifying the person, application, role, reason, and end date where temporary. The system owner approves the role; IT implements it and records evidence. Production administration also needs IT Lead approval. No one approves their own permissions. Temporary access expires within 30 days unless a fresh approval is recorded.

Device baseline
Company data is handled on managed devices with encryption, screen locking within five minutes, automatic updates, endpoint protection, and remote lock or wipe capability. IT inventories devices and checks compliance before granting access. Personal devices may access only approved low-risk services after an explicit, documented IT review; they may not store Restricted data.

Credential handling
Use the approved password manager and unique credentials. Never send passwords or authentication codes through email or chat. Report unexpected authentication prompts, suspected phishing, or exposed secrets immediately. IT rotates affected credentials and assesses scope through INC-09 rather than merely deleting the message.

question: May I paste customer data or confidential source code into a public AI tool?
reference_answer: No; customer data, confidential source code, and personal information must not go into public AI tools or unapproved file-sharing services. Approved AI use must follow service-specific data permissions and a person must check outputs before business use.
required_facts: No; customer data, confidential source code, and personal information must not go into public AI tools or unapproved file-sharing services.
Approved AI use must follow service-specific data permissions and a person must check outputs before business use.

reference_sections.title: Information Security and Access Management
reference_sections.heading: 2. Secure use, changes, and vulnerability handling
reference_sections.text:
Approved tools and data
Install software through IT or the approved catalog. New services require FIN-07 review, including security and privacy checks. Do not place customer data, confidential source code, or personal information into public AI tools or unapproved file-sharing services. Approved AI use must follow the specific data permissions recorded for that service, and a person must check outputs before business use.

Technical maintenance
IT prioritizes actively exploited or internet-exposed critical vulnerabilities for mitigation within 24 hours of confirmation. Other critical vulnerabilities are addressed within seven calendar days; high vulnerabilities within 30 days. If a deadline cannot be met, the IT Lead records compensating controls and seeks a GOV-01 exception before expiry. Active exploitation is handled as an incident, not just a maintenance ticket.

Change procedure
Changes to production require an owner, reason, risk assessment, test evidence, rollback plan, and independent approval. SUP-08 defines release communication. An emergency change may proceed with incident commander approval, but the implementer cannot be the sole approver. Record the change immediately and complete independent review within one business day.

Development practices
Keep secrets out of source code, use peer review, scan dependencies, and test with synthetic or de-identified data wherever possible. Production data in a test environment requires the data owner's and Privacy Lead's written approval and equivalent access controls.

question: What should I do immediately after losing a company laptop, and should I wipe it myself?
reference_answer: Report immediately through the emergency Service Desk channel and notify IT on-call; call the internal on-call number if the channel is unavailable. Do not wipe the device, investigate independently, or delete evidence.
required_facts: Report immediately through the emergency Service Desk channel and notify IT on-call; call the internal on-call number if the channel is unavailable.
Do not wipe the device, investigate independently, or delete evidence.

reference_sections.title: Information Security and Access Management
reference_sections.heading: 3. Reviews, departures, and security reporting
reference_sections.text:
Periodic assurance
System owners review access quarterly, including privileged, temporary, service, and dormant accounts. The reviewer records each account's owner and business need; unnecessary access is removed within two business days, or immediately where risk is urgent. IT reviews privileged access monthly. A completed review requires removal evidence, not just a signed spreadsheet.

Departure procedure
PPL-03 supplies the authorized cutoff time. IT suspends the identity account, revokes active sessions and tokens, removes application access, rotates shared secrets the person knew, and updates the asset register. Business files transfer only to approved custodians. Do not delete a departing worker's records until DAT-06 retention and hold checks are complete.

Report and contain
Report a lost device, suspicious login, malware alert, data exposure, or accidental external sharing immediately through the emergency Service Desk channel and notify the IT on-call contact. If that channel is unavailable, call the published internal on-call number. Disconnect a suspected compromised device from networks if safe, but do not wipe it, investigate independently, or delete evidence.

Records and metrics
Retain access requests and reviews for one year after closure; retain security logs for 90 days unless attached to an incident or hold. Track overdue vulnerabilities, removal timeliness, device compliance, and repeat exceptions monthly. INC-09 governs incident evidence and DAT-06 governs disposal.

question: How long are security logs normally kept, and what if they are under an investigation hold?
reference_answer: Security logs are normally retained for 90 days from creation. A legal, dispute, or investigation hold suspends deletion of affected material until authorized release.
required_facts: Security logs are normally retained for 90 days from creation.
A legal, dispute, or investigation hold suspends deletion of affected material until authorized release.

reference_sections.title: Privacy, Information Handling, and Records
reference_sections.heading: 3. Retention schedule, holds, and disposal
reference_sections.text:
Default internal schedule
Policy versions, approvals, and exceptions: three years after supersession or closure. Conduct cases and safety reports: three years after closure. Employment records: three years after departure. Financial transactions, expenses, and supplier contracts: seven years after transaction or contract end, whichever applies. Customer account records: two years after account closure. Support tickets: two years after closure. Incident records: three years after closure. Continuity plans and exercise records: three years after supersession or exercise. Access requests and reviews: one year after closure. Security logs: 90 days from creation. Unsuccessful applicant records: six months after the hiring decision.

Customer content and backups
Customer-hosted content follows the signed contract's retention and deletion terms. If terms are absent, the Privacy Lead must resolve them before ingestion. Operational backups follow BCP-10's 35-day rolling window and are not a long-term archive. Deleted material may remain in protected backups until rotation; if restored, required deletions must be reapplied before normal use.

Overrides and holds
These are illustrative company defaults, not statements of legal minimums. The Privacy Lead records approved jurisdictional or contractual overrides. A legal, dispute, or investigation hold suspends deletion of affected material until authorized release; record scope, custodian, and release decision.

Disposal procedure
Owners review eligible records monthly, check holds and overrides, and authorize deletion. IT or the records custodian performs secure deletion or approved physical destruction. The disposal log identifies category, date range, method, authorizer, and completion date without copying the deleted content.

question: What approvals and quotes are required for a $6,000 purchase, and may I split it to avoid the threshold?
reference_answer: Manager, Finance, and CEO approval are required in advance. Two comparable quotes or a documented sole-source justification approved by Finance and the CEO are required. Do not split purchases to avoid thresholds.

reference_sections.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
reference_sections.heading: 1. Spending authority and purchasing
reference_sections.text:
Approval matrix
All commitments require advance approval based on total expected value, including taxes, setup, renewals committed by the contract, and related purchases. Up to $500 requires manager approval. Above $500 through $5,000 requires manager and Finance approval. Above $5,000 requires manager, Finance, and CEO approval. Self-approval is prohibited; GOV-01 defines substitute approvers. Budget availability is necessary but does not replace approval.

Purchase request
Before ordering or signing, submit the purpose, supplier, total cost, budget code, alternatives considered, delivery needs, and data or system access implications. Do not split a purchase to fall below a threshold. Recurring contracts are assessed on the full committed term; month-to-month services use projected 12-month cost for approval.

Supplier comparison
Purchases above $5,000 require two comparable quotes or a documented sole-source justification approved by Finance and the CEO. Evaluate suitability, total cost, security, support, and exit terms rather than price alone. Disclose relationships under ETH-02 before participating in selection.

Commitment and receipt
Only a recorded authorized signatory may sign a contract. Finance issues the purchase reference after approvals. The requester confirms goods or services were received and records discrepancies before payment. An invoice is not evidence that the purchase was authorized.

question: When must I submit an expense claim, and what can I do if the receipt is missing?
reference_answer: Submit within 30 calendar days. Provide alternate evidence and a signed explanation for a missing receipt; Finance decides adequacy and documents the decision.
required_facts: Submit within 30 calendar days.
Provide alternate evidence and a signed explanation for a missing receipt; Finance decides adequacy and documents the decision.

reference_sections.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
reference_sections.heading: 3. Expenses, exceptions, and reconciliation
reference_sections.text:
Reimbursable expenses
Reasonable, necessary business costs are reimbursable when approved and supported. Personal purchases, fines, entertainment unrelated to business, and duplicate claims are not reimbursable. Travel follows WRK-04. Obtain approval against the estimated total before incurring costs; the same FIN-07 thresholds apply to reimbursements.

Claim procedure
Submit an expense claim within 30 calendar days with date, vendor, currency, itemized receipt, business purpose, budget code, and prior approval reference. Finance uses a documented conversion source and records the rate. The manager confirms business purpose; Finance checks policy, calculation, and duplication. Claims requiring higher approval must include it before payment. Finance targets payment within ten business days of a complete approved claim.

Missing receipts and urgent costs
For a missing receipt, provide alternate evidence and a signed explanation; Finance decides whether the evidence is adequate and documents the decision. Emergency safety costs may be incurred before approval under WRK-04, then submitted for review the next business day where practicable. Other retrospective requests require a recorded GOV-01 exception and are not automatically reimbursed.

Month-end controls
Finance reconciles bank and card activity monthly, investigates unmatched items, and has an independent reviewer sign off. Track overdue claims, missing approvals, duplicate payments, and supplier concentration. Retain approvals, verification evidence, invoices, claims, and reconciliation records under DAT-06's seven-year financial schedule.

question: What is the P1 acknowledgment target, and does it mean the issue must be resolved by then?
reference_answer: Acknowledge within 30 elapsed minutes and invoke INC-09 immediately. Response means human acknowledgment with an owner and next step, not resolution. Signed customer commitments take precedence over internal targets.
required_facts: Acknowledge within 30 elapsed minutes and invoke INC-09 immediately.
Response means human acknowledgment with an owner and next step, not resolution.
Signed customer commitments take precedence over internal targets.

reference_sections.title: Customer Support and Production Change Procedures
reference_sections.heading: 1. Intake, verification, and service priorities
reference_sections.text:
Support coverage
Routine support operates during GOV-01 business hours. Emergency production incidents are routed to IT on-call at all times. Signed customer commitments take precedence over the internal targets below; Support records any different contract targets on the customer account. Response means a human acknowledgment with an owner and next step, not resolution.

Case intake
Record the customer, verified contact, affected service, symptoms, start time, business impact, safe reproduction steps, and related incident references. Verify authority before discussing account details or changing access. Never request passwords or unrestricted database exports. Restrict attachments containing personal or Confidential information under DAT-06.

Priority targets
P1 is widespread production unavailability or suspected severe data/security impact: acknowledge within 30 elapsed minutes and invoke INC-09 immediately. P2 is major degradation or a blocked customer with no workaround: acknowledge within four business hours. P3 is limited impact with a workaround: acknowledge within one business day. P4 is a question or enhancement: acknowledge within two business days. Reassess priority whenever impact changes.

Ownership
The first assigned agent remains accountable until another owner explicitly accepts handover. Routing a ticket does not discharge responsibility. Support may lower priority only with a recorded impact assessment; a possible security issue must first be assessed by IT.

question: How often must verified internal updates be given during active SEV1 and SEV2 incidents?
reference_answer: The communications lead provides verified internal updates at least hourly for SEV1. SEV2 updates are every four elapsed hours while active, even if investigation continues.
required_facts: The communications lead provides verified internal updates at least hourly for SEV1.
SEV2 updates are every four elapsed hours while active, even if investigation continues.

reference_sections.title: Incident Response and Crisis Communication
reference_sections.heading: 2. Containment, evidence, and external communication
reference_sections.text:
First response
Protect people first, then reduce ongoing harm. Identify affected identities, systems, records, suppliers, and customer groups. Prefer reversible containment such as disabling an account, isolating a device, or revoking a link. Record who authorized each action, when it occurred, and its effect. Emergency production changes follow SEC-05's independent approval rule.

Evidence preservation
Preserve relevant logs, messages, configuration, timestamps, and original files in restricted storage. Record the collector, source, collection time, transfer history, and any changes made during collection. Do not circulate raw evidence in broad chat rooms. The Privacy Lead or authorized adviser may impose a hold under DAT-06; ordinary retention must not delete held evidence.

Communication rules
The communications lead provides a verified internal update at least hourly for SEV1 and every four elapsed hours for SEV2 while active, even if the update is that investigation continues. Support distributes customer updates under SUP-08. The CEO approves public statements; the Privacy Lead coordinates legally or contractually required notices and records applicable deadlines. Approval workflows must not delay a mandatory notice beyond its deadline; escalate immediately to the CEO if timing is at risk.

Working with third parties
Use known supplier contacts, record ticket references, and share only necessary evidence through approved channels. A supplier's assurance does not replace Northstar's impact assessment. Invoke BCP-10 if expected disruption exceeds recovery targets.

question: What are the production customer service RTO and RPO, and are these guarantees?
reference_answer: Production customer service RTO is four hours and RPO is one hour. These are internal planning targets, not guarantees; signed customer commitments may be stricter.
required_facts: Production customer service RTO is four hours and RPO is one hour.
These are internal planning targets, not guarantees; signed customer commitments may be stricter.

reference_sections.title: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
reference_sections.heading: 1. Critical services and recovery objectives
reference_sections.text:
Purpose and activation
Maintain essential customer and workforce operations through loss of technology, a supplier, the office, or key staff. The COO activates continuity when disruption is expected to exceed a recovery objective, normal response capacity is inadequate, or the office becomes unsafe. INC-09 remains the command framework; continuity work supports the same commander rather than creating competing instructions.

Planning objectives
Production customer service has a four-hour recovery time objective and a one-hour recovery point objective. Identity and emergency communication have a four-hour recovery time objective and a 24-hour recovery point objective. Routine support records have an eight-hour recovery time objective and a 24-hour recovery point objective. Finance and People Operations records have a two-business-day recovery time objective and a 24-hour recovery point objective. These are internal planning targets; signed customer commitments may be stricter.

Meaning and dependencies
Recovery time runs from disruption to minimum usable service; recovery point is the maximum targeted age of recoverable data. Neither is a guarantee. IT maps dependencies, including identity, hosting, network, secrets, and suppliers, and ensures prerequisite services can recover early enough to meet dependent service targets.

Ownership
IT maintains technical runbooks, Finance maintains payment alternatives, People Operations maintains worker contact details, and Support maintains customer communication routes. Each critical role has a named deputy in the restricted continuity directory, reviewed quarterly and after staffing changes.

question: Before disposing of an old laptop, what should happen to sensitive data, and may an unauthorized employee speak publicly for the company about it?
reference_answer: Sensitive information must be securely wiped before disposal or reassignment through approved procedures. Only authorized persons may speak officially for the company; unauthorized employees should redirect public questions to the communications lead.
required_facts: Sensitive information must be securely wiped before disposal or reassignment through approved procedures.
Only authorized persons may speak officially for the company; unauthorized employees should redirect public questions to the communications lead.

reference_sections.title: Asset Management and Facility Operations
reference_sections.heading: 8. Disposal and Surplus Management
reference_sections.text:
When an asset reaches the end of useful life, is obsolete, is damaged beyond repair, or is no longer needed, it must be disposed of or redeployed through approved procedures. Disposal may require environmental, finance, or legal review depending on the asset type and value.

Sensitive information stored on devices or equipment must be securely wiped before disposal or reassignment. Physical records and media should be destroyed according to retention and confidentiality requirements.

reference_sections.title: External Communications and Brand Standards
reference_sections.heading: 2. Communication Authority
reference_sections.text:
Only authorized persons may speak on behalf of the company in official external communications. Managers, designated spokespersons, and communications representatives must coordinate with Legal and Marketing or Communications where needed. This requirement is especially important in customer incidents, legal inquiries, media requests, regulatory interactions, and product or service commitments.

Employees who are not designated spokespeople should avoid making public statements that could be interpreted as official company positions. If asked to comment publicly, employees should redirect the question to the appropriate communications lead.
